title: Revision HQ 2.2: programming fundamentals
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Revision HQ 2.2
objectives: know the whole of topic 2.2 well enough to answer without notes
understand the mistakes that most often lose marks in programming questions
know which lessons are secure and which still need revision before the test
starter: Without looking back at your notes, write down the three programming constructs, the five data types, and the four operations a program carries out on a file.

stations.name: Constructs recap
stations.fact: A single equals sign... A double equals sign...
stations.challenge: Write down the difference between = and == and give an example of each.

logic.title: Which of these lines compares two values rather than storing one?
A loop is written as  while lives > 0  but nothing inside it ever changes lives. What happens?

stations.name: Types and operators recap
stations.challenge: Explain what int(7.9) gives, and why that is not the same as rounding.

logic.title: In the OCR Exam Reference Language, what is the value of  "7" + "2" ?

stations.name: File handling recap
stations.fact: The mode a file is opened in decides...
stations.challenge: A program saves a new high score each week, but the file only ever holds one score. Explain what is wrong and how to fix it.

logic.title: A program outputs the first line of a file over and over instead of working through it. Which mistake would cause this?
A program appends a line to a file, but the line is missing when the file is opened again. What is the most likely reason?

stations.name: Records and SQL recap
stations.fact: The part of a query that decides which records come back is...
stations.challenge: Write down the three parts of an SQL query and say what each one decides.

logic.title: A table called Pupils has the fields Name, Year and Choir. Which query returns the names of pupils who are in Year 10 and in the choir?
A query that should find every surname beginning with M returns no records at all. Which line is the problem?

stations.name: Arrays and sub-programs recap
stations.fact: An index goes out of range when...
stations.challenge: An array holds twelve lane numbers. Give the index of the first and of the last, and write the loop that would visit them all.

logic.title: In the OCR Exam Reference Language, which line reads past the end of  array lane[8] ?
A sub-program works out a total correctly, but the main program cannot use the answer. What is missing?

stations.name: Randomness recap
stations.challenge: Explain why random(0, 6) is the wrong call for choosing one of six prizes from an array.

logic.title: In the OCR Exam Reference Language, how many different values can  random(0, 7)  return?
A program sets the seed to the same value every time it starts. What effect does that have?

final.title: Final challenge: the lane draw
final.instr: number the steps in the right order.
rows: Write the finished lane list to a new file
Store the runner's name in the empty lane
If that lane is already taken, pick another number
Pick a random lane number from 0 to 7
Declare an array of eight lanes, all empty
Read the eight runners' names from the file

logic.title: Which techniques does the lane draw program need? Select all that apply.
Why must the program check whether a lane is already taken before it stores a name?

keyq: Which parts of 2.2 am I secure on, and which do I need to revise before the test?
exam: State the difference between a count-controlled loop and a condition-controlled loop.
A club stores its members in a table called Members, with the fields MemberID, Name, Year and Paid. Write an SQL query that returns the name of every member in Year 10 who has not paid.

Eight runners' names are stored in a file. Write an algorithm that gives each runner a different lane from 1 to 8, chosen at random, and outputs the finished draw. Use the OCR Exam Reference Language or a language you know.
confidence: Variables, constants and the three constructs
Data types, casting, operators and string handling
Files, records and SQL, arrays, sub-programs and random numbers
